Run the end-to-end hydrofabric pipeline for a single VPU

Source: R/run_pipeline.R
run_pipeline.Rd

Local convenience wrapper that runs the refactor, aggregate and nextgen phases sequentially on the same filesystem. Each stage is also exported and can be called directly.

Usage

run_pipeline(
  vpuid,
  reference_gpkg,
  fdr_path,
  fac_path,
  fallback_fdr_path = NULL,
  fallback_fac_path = NULL,
  hydrolocations_gpkg = NULL,
  exclude_hl_types = "wbin",
  out_dir = "out",
  from = "refactor",
  through = "nextgen",
  stages = NULL,
  n_cores = NULL,
  skip_if_exists = FALSE,
  verbose = FALSE,
  hydraulics_path = NULL,
  lakes_path = NULL,
  lake_mask_path = NULL,
  slope_parquet = NULL,
  use_checkpoints = FALSE,
  check_input = TRUE,
  ...
)

Arguments

vpuid

VPU identifier (character, e.g. "01", "03N", "21").

reference_gpkg

Path to the reference fabric (multi-VPU or single-VPU; extraction is auto-detected).

fdr_path, fac_path

Paths to the FDR / FAC rasters.

fallback_fdr_path, fallback_fac_path

Optional paths to a fallback FDR/FAC pair. NULL disables fallback (default).

hydrolocations_gpkg

Optional path to a separate GeoPackage holding the hydrolocations (POIs) + pois layers. NULL (default) reads them from reference_gpkg (all-in-one). When supplied, the reference need only carry flowpaths + divides, and POIs are sourced from this file.

exclude_hl_types

Hydrolocation hl_type values to drop before the build sees them. The default removes waterbody INLETS (wbin), 33,926 of the 69,036 supplied locations. An inlet names no computational boundary a consumer asks for, and each one costs twice: it pins its own unit against merging and breaks the levelpath, stranding the unit below it too, which is why they dominate the sub-minimum population.

Waterbody OUTLETS (wbout) are kept. An outlet is a real routing boundary , it is where a lake discharges, so it earns its break in a way an inlet does not. Gages (nwis, rfc) and terminal/coastal outlets (the owp_* types) are kept for the same reason. Lake handling is independent of this either way: lakes come from lakes_path, a separate input.

NULL or character(0) keeps every type. Filtering is by row, so a location carrying a wanted type as well survives on that type.

out_dir

Directory for outputs. A vpu_{vpuid}/ subfolder is created; the stage outputs all land there so this call is backwards-compatible with the monolithic pre-split runs.

from, through

Stage range to run, by name ("refactor", "aggregate", "nextgen", in order). Defaults run the full pipeline. Use through = "aggregate" to stop before the ngen output, or from = "aggregate" to resume from an existing refactored fabric.

stages

Optional integer stage numbers (e.g. c(2, 3)) as an alias for from/through: when supplied, from/through are set to the min/max stage. NULL (default) uses from/through directly.

n_cores

Worker count for parallel steps. Default detectCores() - 2.

skip_if_exists

If TRUE, skip a VPU whose target output (the ngen gpkg when through = "nextgen", otherwise the aggregate output gpkg) already exists. Default FALSE (always rebuild). This is a plain already-built check, not content-hash reuse.

verbose

Pass through to individual steps for extra logging.

hydraulics_path

Optional path to a RiverML channel table parquet, either its v2 output (tw_bf_m, y_bf_m, r_bf, roughness, slope_m_m) or the earlier channel-geometry table. When supplied, routing attributes (flowpath-attributes, flowline-attributes) are computed in Step 6g, and a slope_m_m column also supplies flowpath slope when slope_parquet is NULL. NULL skips Step 6g (default).

lakes_path

Optional path to the NWM lakes GeoPackage; forwarded to nextgen_fabric() (Step 6h). NULL skips lakes (default).

lake_mask_path

Optional path to the lake-mask parquet (reach -> waterbody membership); forwarded to nextgen_fabric(). Required when lakes_path is supplied.

slope_parquet

Optional path to a per-reference-id slope parquet; forwarded to nextgen_fabric(). NULL (default) takes slope from hydraulics_path when that table carries a slope_m_m column, and otherwise leaves slope NA.

use_checkpoints

If TRUE, allow stage checkpoint reuse where supported (currently the refactor phase). Default FALSE recomputes from scratch.

check_input

If TRUE (default), validate the inputs before building: check_reference_input() aborts on damaged identifiers or unresolvable topology, and check_grid_coverage() aborts when a primary grid does not cover the domain, which is what a configuration inheriting another domain's grid looks like.

...

Stage tuning parameters, forwarded to whichever stage declares each (e.g. min_area_sqkm = 5, coverage_min = 0.95). See refactor_fabric(), aggregate_fabric(), nextgen_fabric() for the full set and defaults.

Value

Invisibly, a list with vpuid, status, ngen_gpkg, out_gpkg, timings, invariants, skipped.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
run_pipeline(vpuid          = "01",
             reference_gpkg = "reference_01.gpkg",
             fdr_path       = "fdr.tif",
             fac_path       = "fac.tif",
             out_dir        = "out",
             through        = "nextgen")
} # }
